recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The current source is consistent with FHIR-5248 and later document-page decisions; adding more local prose would be redundant and could drift from the current document-control wording.
issue_request: FHIR-5248 was a Published FHIR-core DSTU1 clarification request for the Documents page. It asked whether statements that a document has a fixed presentation and that its presentation cannot change contradicted stylesheet guidance where the document-specified stylesheet was only a SHOULD.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git-svn commit 4d09a65d3047151c00ef5391e3f7cf61d360da05, matching Jira's SVN revision 4657 comment. That commit added the rule that any referenced or used stylesheet SHALL NOT alter presentation in a way that changes the clinical meaning of the content.
additional_context: Later Published document-page issues refined the same area. FHIR-7388 softened the old cannot-change wording to allow non-substantial presentation differences that do not change clinical meaning. FHIR-8027 adjusted adjacent internal stylesheet wording. FHIR-36636 removed the old immutability/cannot-change paragraph and reframed document changes around frozen resource versions and attestation validity. FHIR-38930 removed remaining unhelpful document-immutability terminology.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/documents.html is in build scope, no longer contains the original absolute presentation-cannot-change wording, defines document presentation as attested content, and preserves the stylesheet SHALL NOT clinical-meaning guardrail plus the document-specified stylesheet SHOULD unless trading partners agree otherwise.
